patch.objective: Physical security controls: bollards, access control vestibule, fencing, video surveillance, security guard, access badge, lighting, and sensors (infrared, pressure, microwave, ultrasonic)
secondaryObjectives: Security control categories (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and control types (preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, compensating, directive)

sources.cite: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Exam Objectives, Version 5.0: 1.2 'Summarize fundamental security concepts', physical security (bollards, access control vestibule, fencing, video surveillance, security guard, access badge, lighting, sensors)
sources.note: The objectives were read for the course and for REQ-231 on 2026-11-11 (a hosted copy of the PDF, through a summarizing fetch); not re-read for this band. The objective title is the course's own wording.

sources.cite: Greene L. QQ: Fire Alarm Release of Electrified Locks. I Dig Hardware (Allegion), 2023-03-06: doors in a means of egress 'must allow free and immediate egress at all times, with a few exceptions'; IBC: 'Loss of power to the lock or locking system shall automatically unlock the electric locks'; delayed egress locks must release on fire alarm and power failure
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of a door-hardware specialist's article on the IBC and NFPA 101; the codes themselves were not read. Used for the rule that access control may restrict entry but never egress.

sources.cite: ASHRAE TC 9.9, Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments (4th edition), as summarized by Upsite Technologies (Ian Seaton, 2019-11-27): recommended inlet temperature 18-27 °C for all classes; allowable class A1 15-32 °C, A2 10-35 °C; the allowable limits 'allow for short operating excursions'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of a vendor blog; the ASHRAE book itself (now in a later edition) was not read. Used for the 27 °C and 32 °C lines only.

The intruder's timeline, the guards' walk, the temperature rise of 0.25 °C a minute with one cooling unit down and the fall with the standby unit are the author's figures for teaching, not measurements.
